title: DoctorOutput
description: The host readiness report `duckduckgo-search-cli doctor` writes on stdout, discriminated by `type: "doctor"`. This is the richest introspection envelope and the one an agent is most likely to parse before deciding whether to attempt a run at all, which is exactly why shipping it with no contract was the costliest of the five gaps closed under GAP-SCHEMA-INTROSPECTION-UNDECLARED-001 in v1.0.3. Read `status` rather than `ok`: `ok` is the legacy hard-only verdict kept for backward compatibility, and a host can be `degraded` while `ok` is still true. Diagnostics are local; nothing here is reported anywhere. English-only: these keys are host diagnostics, not search-result fields.

git_sha.description: Commit the binary was built from. May be empty when built outside a git checkout.

ok.description: LEGACY hard readiness only (chrome detect, config dir, feature). Kept for pre-V15.1 consumers. A soft failure leaves this true, so an agent that reads only `ok` will miss a degraded host — read `status`.

status.description: Agent-first aggregate. `degraded` means every hard check passed but at least one soft check did not.

failed_checks.description: Names of entries in `checks` with `ok: false`, hard and soft alike. Empty when `status` is `healthy`.

strict.description: Whether `--strict` was requested. Under strict, a soft failure also drives a non-zero exit.

chrome_n.description: Chrome-like processes alive on the host. Omitted, not null, when the count could not be taken.

contention_factor_percent.description: Budget multiplier implied by `chrome_n`, as a percentage; 100 means no scaling. Omitted when `chrome_n` is.

ready_for_dual_deep_research.description: Whether a dual-vertical deep-research is advisable on this host WITHOUT raising `--global-timeout`.

recommended_global_timeout.description: Suggested `--global-timeout` for the default dual plus fetch workload on this host, in seconds.

linux_cgroup.description: Linux cgroup opt-in state. `not_applicable` on macOS and Windows; `unavailable` means the operator opted in but the host lacks cgroup v2.

linux_cgroup_memory_max_mb.description: Configured memory ceiling in MiB. Present only when `linux_cgroup` is `enabled`.

environment.description: Runtime markers that change what an operator should expect, such as a container with no display.

labels.description: Human-readable summary of whichever booleans above are set. Empty on a plain host.

chrome.description: Browser detection. Production SERP is Chrome-only over CDP, so `detected: false` means search cannot run at all — it is not a degradation to a plain HTTP path, because none exists.

feature_enabled.description: Whether this binary was compiled with the `chrome` feature. False makes `detected` irrelevant.

path.description: Resolved ELF path. Wrappers and Flatpak entries resolve to the real binary. Null when nothing was found.

channel.description: How the binary was located: `manual` for `--chrome-path` or XDG, otherwise the host packaging.

major_version.description: Major version parsed from `chrome --version`. Null when the probe did not succeed.

error.description: Why detection failed. Null on success.

paths.description: Resolved XDG directories. Null means the platform reported none, which is a finding rather than an error.

severity.description: A failed `hard` check drives `ok: false` and `status: unhealthy`; a failed `soft` check only drives `degraded`.

detail.description: Evidence for the verdict, phrased so the reader can act on it without re-running anything.
